newsitem.title: UK: Europe low sulphur fuel boosted by US swaps buying.
newsitem.headline: Europe low sulphur fuel boosted by US swaps buying.

text.p: Low sulphur fuel prices in Europe were boosted on Thursday by heavy U.S. swaps buying as dealers tried to open the arbitrage window to North America, traders said.
June swaps jumped $3 in the late afternoon as healthy New York Harbor one percent numbers made it theoretically possible to move low sulphur cracked fuel westwards.
"People have been trying to fix cargoes to the States but it's prompt oil they want and Europe is short that at the moment," said one trader. Notional cargo prices lifted to $89/$90 fob a tonne.
At the close of business it was unclear how successful traders had been in putting together large enough parcels to make the voyage profitable. Nor was the extent of June U.S. demand very clear.
In northwest Europe high sulphur barges also jumped as bunker demand picked up dramatically ahead of the Dutch holiday weekend.
Trade began at $83 before rising to a high of $85 a tonne fob, but the bulk of business was at $84.
